data.critique:
Verdict: Not approved — request a specific discriminating analysis.

Why the current call is not justified

  • The direct empirical comparison in the ledger favours the runner-up: the atlas/NSC analysis calls “Protein synthesis” for the active wells, with the 0.3 µM and 3 µM wells both nearest to Protein synthesis and the 4-well tally 3/4 Protein synthesis; no Aurora-kinase neighbour is shown among the leading neighbours. The agent therefore overrode, rather than reconciled, the only direct reference-based MoA evidence provided.
  • The Aurora call rests mainly on the “multinucleate proxy” and irregular/large-nucleus fractions. A proxy is not proof of true multinucleation; cell crowding, segmentation merging, or overlapping nuclei could inflate it. The phenotype description itself is cautious and says composite-only data are insufficient for a confident MoA assignment.
  • Several features are not cleanly Aurora-specific and could also fit Protein synthesis/other stress: average nuclear area and integrated DNA fall dose-dependently, while only a small large-nucleus subset rises; frac_mitotic_like is not increased; tubulin intensity is increased but is non-specific among mitotic/microtubule/stress explanations; and the evidence does not separate Aurora from Eg5 or microtubule mechanisms.
  • The appearance of a threshold between 0.03 µM and 0.3 µM is based on one well per dose. The untested intermediate dose is exactly where a graded Protein-synthesis-like onset could be distinguished from an abrupt mitotic-failure threshold.
  • Accordingly, 0.58 for Aurora kinase inhibitors is over-calibrated given an atlas result pointing the other way and no direct spindle/kinase readout.

Requested experiment (one specific affordable step): acquire dose index 3 (0.1 µM), replicate 1 — the missing intermediate dose between the inactive 0.03 µM well and the fully affected 0.3 µM well — then run the already-used free analyses on that well: dose_response including frac_multinucleate_proxy, nuc_area, frac_large_nucleus, nuc_dna_integrated, tub_mean and cell_count, plus compare_to_reference_atlas. An abrupt switch to strong multinucleation/large nuclei at 0.1 µM with an Aurora-like atlas shift would support the submitted call; a graded intermediate phenotype that remains Protein-synthesis-like would show the runner-up explains the data at least as well and would require downgrading/reversing the conclusion.
data.requested_experiment: Acquire dose index 3 (0.1 µM), replicate 1, then run dose_response (frac_multinucleate_proxy, nuc_area, frac_large_nucleus, nuc_dna_integrated, tub_mean, cell_count) and compare_to_reference_atlas on the enlarged dose series to distinguish an abrupt Aurora-like mitotic-failure threshold from a graded Protein-synthesis-like onset.

data.note:
Re-assessment after unblinding to Epithelial (AZ-J):

Evidence review:
- Profile shows very strong frac_multinucleate_proxy (z 9-13), nuc_eccentricity up, nuc_solidity/form_factor down, frac_large_nucleus up, with dose-threshold between 0.03uM (inactive, z~0) and 0.3uM (z 9), and monotonic nuc_area decrease (rho -1.0) and nuc_dna_integrated decrease (rho -0.8). Microscopist confirms clustering/crowding islands, irregular lobed nuclei, smaller average nuclei with subset large, preserved actin, brighter tubulin diffuse, no assessed spindles.
- Atlas NSC: 3/4 Protein synthesis (sim 0.73-0.75), 1/4 Microtubule destabilizers at low dose (sim 0.77); k-neighbors mixed Epithelial 4/10, Protein synthesis 3/10, Cholesterol-lowering 2/10 at sim ~0.66-0.74. No Aurora neighbour shown. Moderate similarities, not high-confidence.

Does Epithelial make sense?
- Annotated MoA "Epithelial" in BBBC021 is a dataset class for compounds altering epithelial morphology/adhesion (e.g. references AZ-U, PP-2 appearing as neighbours, sim 0.69-0.73). Clustering/islands with gaps, preserved cortical actin, altered cell eccentricity/solidity/roundness are compatible with epithelial junction/cytoskeletal remodeling rather than true mitotic failure.
- Aurora (my call) was based on multinucleate proxy. However: proxy is not ground-truth multinucleation; crowding/segmentation merging from epithelial islands can inflate it, as reviewer noted. PMID 40195468 and PMID 30050055 confirm Aurora A/B inhibition can cause multinucleation/neosis, which motivated the over-call, but classic Aurora also shows increased DNA ploidy and mitotic enrichment. Here nuc_dna_integrated decreases dose-dependently (-2.9 to -4.1), cell_count not strongly reduced, frac_mitotic_like not increased (z -0.5 to -1.2), inconsistent with Aurora polyploid arrest.
- Protein synthesis (atlas favourite) would also explain smaller nuclei and reduced DNA synthesis but not clustering/large-lobed subset; Epithelial at least explains density

reflection.text:
Unblinding: AZ-J, BBBC021 internal code, no PubChem/ChEMBL mechanism - verdict correct=false. Truth: Epithelial. Agent final call: Aurora kinase inhibitors p=0.38 (initial p=0.58). Requested discriminating experiment was not done due to budget exhaustion, and critique was accurate.

What the evidence got right:
The agent correctly measured a strong dose-dependent nuclear shape phenotype: frac_multinucleate_proxy z=+9.0 at 0.3uM (e2), +10.9 at 1uM (e7), +13.0 at 3uM (e3), with nuc_eccentricity +7.5 to +9.2 and decreasing nuc_major_axis z=-7.3 to -9.0, plus dose_response rho=+1.00 p=0 for that proxy (e8/e17) and rho=-1.00 p=0 for nuc_area (e12/e18). Initial hypotheses and the review correctly flagged the tension: atlas NSC 2/2 then 3/4 Protein synthesis (e5, e11, e20) vs morphology suggesting mitotic failure, and downgraded from 0.58 to 0.38 while adding Epithelial 0.08 in step 24. The proposal for phospho-Aurora/phospho-H3 and spindle imaging was the right orthogonal test for a proxy.

What misled and why:
1. Proxy != proof. The Aurora call rested on frac_multinucleate_proxy and frac_large_nucleus (+6.3z e2, rho +0.80 e13/e19). As review noted, microscopist e4 explicitly said composite-only data are insufficient for confident MoA and listed candidates as unknown with only density lower. Crowding, eccentricity (+7.5z), and segmentation merging can inflate this proxy. True multinucleation was never confirmed.

2. Direct comparison was overridden. NSC vote never favored Aurora: 2/2 and 3/4 Protein synthesis, k-neighbours Epithelial 3/10 then 4/10 (e5, e11, e20). Agent discounted this because similarity ~0.74 felt modest, anchoring early on mitotic failure after e2/e3. Truth was the k-neighbour second-place class. Final hypotheses still weighted Epithelial only 0.08 despite it being the leading neighbour pool (4/10) - miscalibrated.

3. Contradictory dose trends were underweighted. nuc_area falling (rho -1.00), nuc_dna_integrated falling rho -0.80 (e14/e21), cell_count rho -0.40 p=0.6 (e10/e23) with frac_mitotic_like not increased, and tub_mean rho +0.80 p=0.2 non-specific (e9/e22). A true Aurora polyploidy should increase integrated DNA in a large-nucleus subset, not decrease average DNA. The pattern fits heterogeneous epithelial size/shape remodeling with lower density (e4) better than mitotic failure.

4. Early epithelial cytoskeletal signal ignored. At the inactive low-intermediate dose 0.03uM (e6) where multinucleate proxy is absent, act_tub_ratio z=+3.6, cell_eccentricity +2.1, cell_solidity -1.0 already deviated. That graded actin/shape onset is expected for Epithelial class (EMT/shape remodeling, e.g. PMID 33328637 describes epithelial hybrid states; PMID 41879555 and PMID 33115917 discuss epithelial functional states) rather than an abrupt 0.03 to 0.3uM mitotic threshold. Agent noted e6 but did not integrate it.

5. Acquisition choice caused the impasse. Plan was mid/high dose first (e2-e3), then 0.03uM and 1uM (e6-e7) - spending all 4 wells as one well per dose. This left the critical threshold dose 0.1uM (dose index 3) untested and no replicates to test rho=+1.00 robustness. When review requested exactly that intermediate dose plus dose_response and atlas on the enlarged series, agent could only re-run same 4-well analyses (e17-e23) with budget spent. Literature search for 'Aurora inhibitor multinucleation' (e27) returns expected associations - e.g. PMID 30050055 multinucleation after AURORA-A loss, PMID 18716057 Aurora B in retinal epithelial cells for chromosome segregation/cytokinesis, PMID 40195468 and PMID 38992487 on Aurora inhibitor senescence/neosis - but these explain plausibility, not discrimination; they may have reinforced confirmation bias without providing compound-specific support, and no PMID supports AZ-J as Aurora.

Lesson: when a proxy drives a call against the atlas, hold probability low until proxy is validated by spindle/kinase readout, conserve budget for the intermediate threshold dose and replicates, and weight consistent k-neighbour epithelial actin/eccentricity signals (e6, e11/e20) rather than treating decreasing nuc_area and DNA as confirmatory for Aurora.
what_was_right: Strong dose-dependent nuclear eccentricity/multinucleate-proxy signal detected across 0.3-3uM (e2,e3,e7) with rho=+1.0
Atlas vs morphology conflict recognized and confidence downgraded 0.58 to 0.38
what_was_wrong: Called Aurora 0.58/0.38 despite NSC 3/4 Protein synthesis and leading k-neighbour Epithelial 4/10 (e11,e20) - overrode direct comparison
Treated frac_multinucleate_proxy as true multinucleation without imaging confirmation despite cautious e4
Ignored contradictory trends: nuc_area and nuc_dna_integrated decreasing while only small large-nucleus subset increasing
Ignored low-dose actin/shape signal e6 suggesting graded epithelial remodeling before proxy onset
Spent budget on 4 single wells across doses, leaving requested 0.1uM threshold dose and replicates untested

Verdict: Not approved — request a specific discriminating analysis.

Why the current call is not justified

  • The direct empirical comparison in the ledger favours the runner-up: the atlas/NSC analysis calls “Protein synthesis” for the active wells, with the 0.3 µM and 3 µM wells both nearest to Protein synthesis and the 4-well tally 3/4 Protein synthesis; no Aurora-kinase neighbour is shown among the leading neighbours. The agent therefore overrode, rather than reconciled, the only direct reference-based MoA evidence provided.
  • The Aurora call rests mainly on the “multinucleate proxy” and irregular/large-nucleus fractions. A proxy is not proof of true multinucleation; cell crowding, segmentation merging, or overlapping nuclei could inflate it. The phenotype description itself is cautious and says composite-only data are insufficient for a confident MoA assignment.
  • Several features are not cleanly Aurora-specific and could also fit Protein synthesis/other stress: average nuclear area and integrated DNA fall dose-dependently, while only a small large-nucleus subset rises; frac_mitotic_like is not increased; tubulin intensity is increased but is non-specific among mitotic/microtubule/stress explanations; and the evidence does not separate Aurora from Eg5 or microtubule mechanisms.
  • The appearance of a threshold between 0.03 µM and 0.3 µM is based on one well per dose. The untested intermediate dose is exactly where a graded Protein-synthesis-like onset could be distinguished from an abrupt mitotic-failure threshold.
  • Accordingly, 0.58 for Aurora kinase inhibitors is over-calibrated given an atlas result pointing the other way and no direct spindle/kinase readout.

Requested experiment (one specific affordable step): acquire dose index 3 (0.1 µM), replicate 1 — the missing intermediate dose between the inactive 0.03 µM well and the fully affected 0.3 µM well — then run the already-used free analyses on that well: dose_response including frac_multinucleate_proxy, nuc_area, frac_large_nucleus, nuc_dna_integrated, tub_mean and cell_count, plus compare_to_reference_atlas. An abrupt switch to strong multinucleation/large nuclei at 0.1 µM with an Aurora-like atlas shift would support the submitted call; a graded intermediate phenotype that remains Protein-synthesis-like would show the runner-up explains the data at least as well and would require downgrading/reversing the conclusion.
